airport.name: Béchar Boudghene Ben Ali Lotfi Airport

summary: Béchar Boudghene Ben Ali Lotfi Airport (CBH) serves the city of Béchar in western Algeria, a strategic gateway to the Algerian Sahara near the Moroccan border. The airport is named after Boudghene Ben Ali Lotfi, a revered figure in Algerian national history. It provides essential connectivity for the remote desert region, supporting both civilian travel and military operations given its proximity to key Saharan routes.
faqs:
Q: How far is the airport from Béchar city center?
A: The airport is located just a few kilometers south of Béchar, typically a 15-20 minute drive depending on traffic.

Q: What airlines operate at Béchar Airport?
A: The airport is primarily served by Air Algérie, with regular domestic flights connecting to Algiers and other major Algerian cities.

Q: Does the airport have international flights?
A: It mostly handles domestic routes, though occasional regional flights to neighboring North African destinations may be available.

Q: Is the airport open 24 hours?
A: Operating hours are aligned with scheduled flight times, and the terminal is generally open during flight arrivals and departures rather than around the clock.
transport_tips: Taxis are readily available outside the terminal and offer the most convenient way to reach Béchar city center. Shared taxi (collective) services are also an affordable option for travelers familiar with the area. Renting a car in advance is recommended for those planning to explore the surrounding Saharan region.
local_tip: Bring layers—even in spring and fall, desert evenings near Béchar can turn surprisingly cold due to the high-altitude desert climate, so have a jacket ready when stepping off the plane.
